titleEn: ‘Bring us your difficult trait problems’: Biographica, Hudson River partner on crop genome editing
titleZh: Biographica与Hudson River合作推进作物基因组编辑
summaryZh: 英国初创公司Biographica与荷兰基因组编辑专家Hudson River Biotechnology达成合作，将Biographica的AI预测平台与Hudson River的编辑和再生能力结合，从靶点发现到商业化编辑品种，为育种者提供解决疑难性状问题的全链条服务。初期聚焦番茄，后拓展至其他作物。该模式尤其适用于传统靶点耗尽、数据不足或需绕开专利的情况。
featuredReason: 虽然本文聚焦作物基因组编辑而非畜牧，但其AI驱动的基因靶点预测与编辑设计平台，对畜牧育种（如抗病育种、性状改良）具有跨领域借鉴意义，尤其适合关注AI+基因组学在农业应用的从业者。
contentFull:
UK startup Biographica and Dutch genome editing specialist Hudson River Biotechnology are partnering to take crop trait development from target discovery through to edited commercial varieties.

The collaboration combines Biographica’s computational platform for identifying high-value gene targets associated with traits from disease resistance to drought tolerance, with Hudson River’s genome-editing, transformation and regeneration capabilities.

The partners will initially focus on tomatoes before expanding into other crops.

“Hudson River has deep expertise in genome editing, and to serve a wider variety of customers, they can leverage our predictive capabilities such that a customer can say ‘I have this trait problem, give me an edited variety to solve that,” Biographica cofounder Dominic Hall, PhD, told AgFunderNews.

Through the new model, he said, “We anticipate customers would approach Hudson River, which would then leverage Biographica’s predictive capabilities to nominate priority genes to generate edits for.”

How it works

Biographica uses its platform to identify the genes associated with a desired trait, ranks them according to their likelihood of working in a particular crop, and designs the edits. Hudson River would then deploy those changes using its BioMaas editing and single-cell regeneration workflow.

The model is particularly useful where obvious genetic targets have already been exhausted, where there is insufficient data to identify a good target, or where companies need to work around existing intellectual property, said Hall, who cofounded Biographica in 2022 with Cecily Price.

The partnership does not necessarily target companies that lack their own discovery or transformation capabilities but gives breeders additional capacity to pursue projects outside their core programs.

“It’s a case of bring us your most difficult trait problems,” said Hall. These could include “a trait problem where they don’t really have the data to solve it that well right now” or cases where a company is “blocked by existing patents and they need to find a way to generate traits that go around that.”

Under the commercial arrangement, a customer coming through Hudson River would remain Hudson River’s customer, while Hudson and Biographica would share costs behind the scenes and any upside generated by a project, said Hall.

“Hudson River is one of very few companies that can edit crops as difficult as strawberry, transgene-free and at a scale our clients depend on. Put those together and a customer can bring us a trait problem and get the whole way to a plant, which is not something either of us could offer alone.”

“By bringing our capabilities together, we want to move genome editing beyond the obvious targets and unlock traits that breeding has not yet been able to crack.” Lotte Westerhof, CSO, Hudson River Biotechnology

Dominic Hall: “Hudson River is one of very few companies that can edit crops as difficult as strawberry, transgene-free and at a scale our clients depend on.” Image credit: Hudson River Biotechnology
The discovery bottleneck

To identify targets for edits, said Hall, many firms still rely on Genome-Wide Association Studies (GWAS) that scan the genomes of many plants and statistically link DNA variants to traits by analyzing which variants show up most often in plants with the trait.

Quantitative Trait Loci (QTL) mapping, in turn, crosses plants with different traits and tracks how DNA regions and the trait are inherited together in offspring, which narrows down regions of the genome likely influencing the trait.

The challenge, said Hall, is that these approaches prove correlation, not causation, and do not prioritize or rank genetic targets or “hits.”

Biographica’s platform, by contrast, deploys multi-modal machine learning to predict which genes are most influential, how they interact with others, and which are likely to be the best targets for gene editing with fewer unwanted side effects.

At the root of this are foundation models trained on multi-modal genomic datasets that capture both gene/gene and gene/trait interactions. The models then predict genes most likely to causally impact a trait and then design edits accordingly. Experimental results are then fed back into the models, delivering continuous improvement.

Susceptibility genes

In addition to identifying novel genetic targets, Biographica is also pursuing complex edit design approaches. Rather than simply switching genes on or off through knockouts, for example, it is developing models designed to predict how genetic edits could alter gene expression in different tissues, contexts or in response to different stimuli.

This is enabling more nuanced engineering of so-called susceptibility genes that pathogens exploit to infect plants, but which can also play an important role in normal plant development, so knocking them out impose yield or developmental penalties.

Instead, said Hall, “We ask can we modulate expression of these genes in specific contexts so we can reduce the susceptibility of the plant without having yield a penalty? That’s a core focus area for us at the moment.”

While for many customers, a straightforward knockout may still be the most appropriate approach, Biographica and Hudson River are exploring this more advanced form of editing, including changes to regulatory DNA that controls when and where a gene is active, he added.

Focusing on susceptibility genes (as opposed to resistance genes) could also provide more durable forms of disease resistance, said Hall, although he was careful not to make sweeping claims.

‘Guided by market pull’

In addition to its partnership work with large clients such as BASF, Biographica is also working on trait development in-house, said Hall, who recently raised a £7 million ($9.5 million) seed round led by Faber VC.

“In all cases, these bets will be guided by market pull. For these deep trait bets, as well as considering simple gene knock-outs, Biographica is also pursuing more complex and subtle edit design approaches. Given Hudson River’s established expertise in genome editing, as well as pursuing some transformation and editing work in-house, Biographica and HRB will be exploring these complex edit design approaches to bring the most promising and valuable traits to market.

Right now, disease resistance is the strongest signal from breeders and other potential customers, he said. But there are also opportunities in crop quality and nutrition.

translationZh:
英国初创公司Biographica与荷兰基因组编辑专家Hudson River Biotechnology正在合作，将作物性状开发从靶点发现推进到编辑后的商业化品种。

该合作将Biographica用于识别与抗病性、耐旱性等性状相关的高价值基因靶点的计算平台，与Hudson River的基因组编辑、转化和再生能力相结合。

合作方最初将聚焦番茄，随后扩展至其他作物。

Biographica联合创始人Dominic Hall博士对AgFunderNews表示：“Hudson River在基因组编辑方面拥有深厚专长，为了服务更广泛的客户，他们可以利用我们的预测能力，这样客户就可以说‘我有这个性状问题，给我一个编辑品种来解决它’。”

他说，通过这种新模式，“我们预计客户会联系Hudson River，后者随后利用Biographica的预测能力来提名优先基因以生成编辑。”

**运作方式**

Biographica利用其平台识别与目标性状相关的基因，根据其在特定作物中起作用的可能性进行排序，并设计编辑方案。Hudson River随后利用其BioMaas编辑和单细胞再生工作流部署这些改变。

Hall表示，该模式在明显遗传靶点已被穷尽、数据不足以识别良好靶点、或公司需要绕开现有知识产权的情况下尤为有用。Hall与Cecily Price于2022年共同创立了Biographica。

该合作并不一定针对缺乏自身发现或转化能力的公司，而是为育种者提供额外能力，以推进其核心项目之外的项目。

Hall说：“这就是‘把你最困难的性状问题交给我们’。”这些问题可能包括“他们目前确实没有足够数据来解决的性状问题”，或者公司“被现有专利阻挡，需要找到绕开的方法来生成性状”。

Hall表示，在商业安排下，通过Hudson River来的客户仍然是Hudson River的客户，而Hudson和Biographica将在幕后分担成本并共享项目产生的任何收益。

“Hudson River是少数几家能够编辑像草莓这样困难的作物、无需转基因且达到客户依赖的规模的公司之一。把这些结合在一起，客户可以带着性状问题来找我们，一路得到植株，这是我们任何一方单独都无法提供的。”

“通过将我们的能力结合在一起，我们希望将基因组编辑推向显而易见的靶点之外，解锁育种尚未能攻克的性状。”——Hudson River Biotechnology首席科学官Lotte Westerhof

Dominic Hall：“Hudson River是少数几家能够编辑像草莓这样困难的作物、无需转基因且达到客户依赖的规模的公司之一。”图片来源：Hudson River Biotechnology

**发现瓶颈**

Hall表示，为了识别编辑靶点，许多公司仍然依赖全基因组关联研究（GWAS），即扫描大量植物的基因组，通过分析哪些变异在具有该性状的植物中出现最频繁，将DNA变异与性状进行统计关联。

数量性状位点（QTL）作图则通过杂交具有不同性状的植物，追踪DNA区域和性状如何在后代中一起遗传，从而缩小可能影响性状的基因组区域。

Hall说，挑战在于这些方法证明的是相关性而非因果关系，并且不会对遗传靶点或“命中”进行优先级排序。

相比之下，Biographica的平台部署多模态机器学习来预测哪些基因影响最大、它们如何相互作用，以及哪些可能是最佳基因编辑靶点且副作用更少。

其核心是在多模态基因组数据集上训练的基础模型，这些数据集捕获基因-基因和基因-性状相互作用。模型随后预测最可能因果影响性状的基因，并据此设计编辑。实验结果随后反馈到模型中，实现持续改进。

**感病基因**

除了识别新的遗传靶点外，Biographica还在探索复杂的编辑设计方法。例如，不是简单地通过敲除来开启或关闭基因，它正在开发模型来预测遗传编辑如何在不同组织、背景或响应不同刺激时改变基因表达。

这使得对所谓感病基因进行更精细的工程改造成为可能——病原体利用这些基因感染植物，但这些基因也可能在正常植物发育中发挥重要作用，因此敲除它们会带来产量或发育惩罚。

Hall说：“相反，我们问能否在特定背景下调节这些基因的表达，从而降低植物的感病性而不产生产量惩罚？这是我们目前的核心关注领域。”

他补充说，虽然对许多客户来说，简单的敲除可能仍是最合适的方法，但Biographica和Hudson River正在探索这种更高级的编辑形式，包括改变控制基因何时何地活跃的调控DNA。

Hall说，聚焦感病基因（而非抗病基因）还可能提供更持久的抗病形式，不过他谨慎地没有做出笼统的断言。

**“由市场拉动引导”**

Hall表示，除了与BASF等大客户的合作外，Biographica也在进行内部性状开发。他最近完成了由Faber VC领投的700万英镑（950万美元）种子轮融资。

“在所有情况下，这些押注都将由市场拉动引导。对于这些深度性状押注，除了考虑简单的基因敲除外，Biographica还在探索更复杂和精细的编辑设计方法。鉴于Hudson River在基因组编辑方面的成熟专长，以及内部进行的一些转化和编辑工作，Biographica和HRB将探索这些复杂的编辑设计方法，将最有前景和价值的性状推向市场。”

他说，目前抗病性是育种者和其他潜在客户发出的最强信号。但在作物品质和营养方面也存在机会。
